# Perseus Vault

Persistent, encrypted, deterministic memory for AI agents. Local-first and MCP-native.

## MCP tools

### perseus-vault

Path: `/vault/mcp-reference/mcp-tools.html`
Version: 2.23.1

Persistent, encrypted, deterministic memory for AI agents. Local-first and MCP-native.

#### Operations

##### TOOL perseus_vault_remember

Summary: Remember Entity

Store or update an entity by (category, key). Idempotent — call as often as you want, same key returns an update. NEAR-DUPLICATE MERGING (#531): a NEW key whose body is >=70% trigram-similar to an existing entity in the same category+workspace does NOT create a new entity — the write is folded into the existing one (result: action='deduped', deduped=true, merged_into=<id>). Right for conversational memory; wrong for bulk ingest of templated records, which are similar by construction and will silently collapse to a handful of rows. For bulk ingest pass skip_dedup=true (or use perseus_vault_ingest_file), and check the returned action. Prefer recall_when triggers (retrieve when relevant) over always_on=true (inject unconditionally): the recall-first perseus_vault_context hard-caps the always-on set and warns when it overflows, so reserve always_on for genuinely identity-critical facts. Optional certainty (0.0-1.0) is used by perseus_vault_conflicts for typed-entity conflict detection. Pass derived_from (ids or {category,key} pairs of the memories you recalled) to auto-mark those sources useful — cited memories rank higher and decay slower. Use this for saving facts, decisions, architecture notes, and conventions. Optional hints (#919): 1-3 prospective query phrasings that should retrieve this entity (vocabulary-gap recall) — indexed into FTS5 alongside the body, default-off (PERSEUS_VAULT_HINTS_ENABLED=1 to enable), replaced wholesale on update. When encryption is enabled, body_json is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.

Request body: application/json

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "name": "action",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "'created' for new entities, 'updated' for existing ones"
    },
    "admission": {
      "name": "admission",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Hash-covered, content-minimized admission evidence."
    },
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entity category"
    },
    "derived_from": {
      "name": "derived_from",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Present when derived_from citations were passed: {reinforced: n, not_found: [labels]}"
    },
    "disposition": {
      "name": "disposition",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Existing detailed disposition, such as quarantined; use outcome_class for stable aggregation."
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entity ID, e.g. 'mem-a1b2c3d4e5f6'"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entity key"
    },
    "outcome_class": {
      "name": "outcome_class",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Stable four-way admission result. SAVE is durably active; DROP and BLOCK are non-persisting terminal decisions; PENDING_APPROVAL is retained but non-serveable until review.",
      "enum": [
        "save",
        "drop",
        "block",
        "pending_approval"
      ]
    },
    "proposed": {
      "name": "proposed",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when the write lacks authoritative admission and must remain reviewable."
    },
    "provenance": {
      "name": "provenance",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Hash-only admission/provenance state; raw prompts, bodies, credentials, and tool arguments are excluded."
    },
    "requires_review": {
      "name": "requires_review",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Whether the stored write must be reviewed before promotion or authoritative use."
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_write_gate

Summary: Write Gate

#939 zero-token write gate: deterministic keep/supersede/forget BEFORE LLM enrichment. Read-only precheck over (category, key, body) that decides store / duplicate / supersede / forget / adjudicate from content-hash + stored-signature near-duplicate scans and an importance floor — ZERO LLM tokens. Only 'adjudicate' (a near-duplicate that may be a contradiction) should escalate to the LLM or operator review. Call this before the enrichment pass to cut per-write Ollama load.

Parameters:
- `body_json` (argument, string, required) - Serialized body of the candidate write.
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category of the candidate write.
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key of the candidate write.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Optional workspace scope for the scans.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_provider_source_event

Summary: Provider Source Event

Apply a versioned provider-native source event. Preserves stable provider identity, revision and content digests, timestamps, thread or parent lineage, visibility and workspace scope, and governed deletion tombstones. The envelope never accepts or stores raw provider bodies or payloads. Replaying the same provider/external_id/revision is idempotent.

Parameters:
- `author` (argument, string, optional)
- `canonical_uri` (argument, string, optional)
- `capture_method` (argument, string, optional)
- `content_sha256` (argument, string, optional)
- `entity_id` (argument, string, optional)
- `event_type` (argument, string, required)
- `expected_revision` (argument, string, optional)
- `external_id` (argument, string, required)
- `kind` (argument, string, required)
- `observed_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional)
- `parent_id` (argument, string, optional)
- `provider` (argument, string, required)
- `provider_created_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional)
- `provider_event_id` (argument, string, optional)
- `provider_updated_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped identity; caller-supplied values are overwritten.
- `retention_policy` (argument, string, optional)
- `revision` (argument, string, required)
- `schema_version` (argument, integer, required)
- `source_span_ref` (argument, string, optional)
- `thread_id` (argument, string, optional)
- `visibility` (argument, string, optional)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "entity_archived": {
      "name": "entity_archived",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "event_id": {
      "name": "event_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "event_type": {
      "name": "event_type",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "outcome": {
      "name": "outcome",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "applied",
        "idempotent",
        "revision_race",
        "deleted"
      ]
    },
    "previous_revision": {
      "name": "previous_revision",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "receipt_digest": {
      "name": "receipt_digest",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "schema_version": {
      "name": "schema_version",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "source": {
      "name": "source",
      "type": "object"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_declared_graph_manifest

Summary: Declared Graph Manifest

Apply a versioned, source-keyed declared graph manifest. Stable node and edge IDs are scoped by workspace and canonical identity; replace revisions supersede prior active topology, while delete revisions create tombstones and preserve history. Declared edges remain sourced or supported until explicitly attested. No LLM extraction is performed.

Request body: application/json

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "edge_ids": {
      "name": "edge_ids",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "edges": {
      "name": "edges",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "manifest_id": {
      "name": "manifest_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "node_ids": {
      "name": "node_ids",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "outcome": {
      "name": "outcome",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "applied",
        "idempotent"
      ]
    },
    "schema_version": {
      "name": "schema_version",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "source_id": {
      "name": "source_id",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "schema_version",
    "outcome",
    "manifest_id",
    "source_id",
    "node_ids",
    "edge_ids",
    "edges"
  ]
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_declared_graph_attest

Summary: Attest Declared Graph Edges

Explicitly attest selected active declared edges under an authority reference. Sourced or supported edges cannot become attested through ingestion alone; the selected edge IDs, manifest revision, attestor, and bounded reference are recorded and replay is idempotent.

- `attested_by` (argument, string, required)
- `edge_ids` (argument, array, required)

- `revision` (argument, string, required)
- `schema_version` (argument, integer, required)
- `source_key` (argument, string, required)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, required)

```json
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "manifest_id": {
      "name": "manifest_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "outcome": {
      "name": "outcome",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "applied",
        "idempotent"
      ]
    },
    "receipt_digest": {
      "name": "receipt_digest",
      "type": "string"

    "receipt_digest"

```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_declared_graph_query

Summary: Query Declared Graph

Read a bounded workspace-scoped projection of declared graph nodes and edges. Active-only output is the default; include_history exposes superseded and tombstoned revisions. Every edge carries source revision, digest/span, scope, origin, validity, and explicit attestation state. This is separate from ordinary recall and does not add graph traversal cost to normal queries.

Parameters:
- `include_history` (argument, boolean, optional)
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped identity; caller-supplied values are overwritten.
- `source_key` (argument, string, optional)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, required)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "edges": {
      "name": "edges",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "nodes": {
      "name": "nodes",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "schema_version": {
      "name": "schema_version",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "source_key": {
      "name": "source_key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "truncated": {
      "name": "truncated",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "workspace_hash": {
      "name": "workspace_hash",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "schema_version",
    "workspace_hash",
    "nodes",
    "edges",
    "truncated"
  ]
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_recall

Summary: Recall Entities

Search entities with FTS5 keyword search. Words are OR'd together. Returns entities sorted by relevance with expanded content/summary fields at top level. Use this to find previously stored facts, decisions, or architecture notes. When encryption is enabled, body_json is decrypted transparently.

Request body: application/json

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "abstain_hint": {
      "name": "abstain_hint",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "#917: true only when a high-confidence direct contradiction is present in the delivered set"
    },
    "conflict_flags": {
      "name": "conflict_flags",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "#917: optional deterministic contradiction/supersession/staleness flags; IDs, validity ranges, and hash-linked evidence refs only",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "conflict_flags_markdown": {
      "name": "conflict_flags_markdown",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "#917: optional ID/hash/validity-only markdown rendering of conflict flags"
    },
    "declared_graph": {
      "name": "declared_graph",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "#1142: optional bounded declared graph projection; nodes/edges carry hash-only source, span, scope, origin, validity, and support state."
    },
    "evidence": {
      "name": "evidence",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "#1135: optional governed derived/verbatim evidence projection with shared budget, exclusions, source groups, and hash-only receipt. Present only when evidence_lanes is supplied."
    },
    "fused_trace": {
      "name": "fused_trace",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "#883: fused serving trace. When include_selection_decisions=true it contains selection_decisions: a bounded hash-only projection of candidate eligibility, dispositions, arm states, token estimates, delivered order, and replay fingerprint."
    },
    "items": {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Matching entities with expanded body_json fields at top level",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "total": {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of results returned"
    },
    "variants": {
      "name": "variants",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of query variants used when expansion is enabled"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_handoff_pack

Summary: Handoff Pack

Budgeted handoff pack: lifecycle-filtered (expired/superseded excluded), provenance-tagged context for cross-session handoffs under a hard token budget, with exclusion visibility and a deterministic pack digest. Candidates from FTS5 recall; greedy-with-backfill packing; never exceeds budget_tokens. Optional planning-boundary enrichment (#1039): include_intent_trail adds recent journal events tied to the pack, include_next_work adds journal forward plans plus recall_when anticipation matches, include_conflicts adds pack-scoped contradiction flags.

Parameters:
- `budget_tokens` (argument, integer, optional) - Hard pack budget in tokens (chars/4), 100..100000, default 2000
- `include_conflicts` (argument, boolean, optional) - Add pack-scoped contradiction flags from the conflict detector (default false)
- `include_expired` (argument, boolean, optional) - Include expired checkable claims (default false)
- `include_intent_trail` (argument, boolean, optional) - Add intent_trail: recent journal events tied to the packed entities (default false)
- `include_next_work` (argument, boolean, optional) - Add next_work: journal forward plans + recall_when anticipation matches for the scope (default false)
- `max_excluded` (argument, integer, optional) - Max excluded items listed with reasons, 0..200, default 20
- `max_trail` (argument, integer, optional) - Max intent-trail events to return, 1..20, default 5
- `query` (argument, string, required) - Handoff topic query (required, non-empty)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope hash. When set, the pack and its enrichment are scoped to that workspace.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_delegation_brief

Summary: Delegation Brief

Deterministic markdown delegation brief generated at the planning boundary (#1039): goal + scope + binding context (superseded items excluded and listed as do-not-resurrect) + intent trail + next work + output contract. Hand a subagent the brief instead of the parent chat session; the brief is self-contained for the delegated task.

Parameters:
- `budget_tokens` (argument, integer, optional) - Hard brief budget in tokens (chars/4), 200..100000, default 4000
- `goal` (argument, string, required) - One-sentence goal of the delegated task (required, non-empty)
- `include_expired` (argument, boolean, optional) - Include expired checkable claims in binding context (default false)
- `output_contract` (argument, string, optional) - Exact output the delegate must produce (files, commands, report shape). Omitted = return a plan with explicit open questions.
- `query` (argument, string, required) - Scope anchor query for the delegation (required, non-empty)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope hash. When set, the brief is built only from that workspace.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_intention

Summary: Intention Program

Prospective memory: typed intention programs (Latch borrow) with immutable revisions, compound triggers/inhibitors, time windows, approval flags, atomic exactly-once claims (JSON1 compare-and-set), and purpose-based forgetting. Ops: create|update (new immutable revision), evaluate (waiting|ready|blocked|expired + reasons), claim (exactly-once), complete|fail (one-shot auto-forgets), list.

Parameters:
- `claimed_by` (argument, string, optional) - Claimer identity for the claim op
- `name` (argument, string, optional) - Intention name (required for all ops except list)
- `note` (argument, string, optional) - Outcome note for complete/fail
- `op` (argument, string, required) - Operation
- `program` (argument, object, optional) - Instruction: {when:{triggers:[{query}]}, unless:{inhibitors:[{query}]}, window:{after_unix_ms?,before_unix_ms?}, action:{kind,params}, approval:'required'|'auto'}
- `purpose` (argument, string, optional) - one_shot auto-forgets on completion (default one_shot)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_proof_frame

Summary: Proof Frame

Proof frame: bounded, hash-cited evidence pack for external consumers (Qorx Zero borrow). Memory stays on-device; the consumer gets only a capped frame (top-N records + per-record source hashes + frame digest). Empty frame -> refusal, never invention. zeroize:true permanently blanks framed entities' bodies after framing (privacy end-state).

Parameters:
- `max_chars` (argument, integer, optional) - Max frame chars, 200..20000, default 1600
- `max_records` (argument, integer, optional) - Max records in the frame, 1..20, default 5
- `query` (argument, string, required) - Evidence question (required, non-empty)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope hash
- `zeroize` (argument, boolean, optional) - Blank framed entities' bodies after framing (default false)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_recall_batch

Summary: Recall Entities Batch

Recall entities across a batch of queries, fusing their results server-side using reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) to merge, deduplicate, and surface the most globally relevant memories first.

Request body: application/json

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "items": {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Matching entities fused from batch queries with expanded body_json fields at top level",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "total": {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of results returned"
    }
  }
}
```

Recall entities from a specific biomimetic memory layer (world, episodic, semantic).

- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum number of results to return (max 1000).
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped requester identity used for visibility enforcement.

Returns:
```json

  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "items": {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Matching entities with expanded body_json fields at top level.",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "total": {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of results returned."
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_scan

Summary: Scan / Enumerate Entities

Enumerate every entity in a category (or the whole store) deterministically, page by page (#562). This is the first-class 'list all / export / sync / reset' path: pages are keyed by immutable entity id (ascending) with a continuation cursor, so repeated calls walk the full set exactly once — unlike recall(query="") pagination, whose relevance ordering mutates as recalls reinforce entities (pages can skip or repeat rows) and whose offset is capped. Call with no cursor for the first page, then pass back next_cursor until has_more is false. Read-only: scanning does not bump retrieval counts or decay. Note the recall query contract this complements: recall's query="" is match-all enumeration; "*" is a literal FTS5 term (NOT a glob) and matches nothing.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Category to enumerate, e.g. 'decision'. Omit or pass "" to scan every category (no category is excluded — unlike recall, which hides high-volume categories such as 'conversation' unless explicitly requested).
- `cursor` (argument, string, optional) - Continuation cursor: the next_cursor value from the previous page. Omit for the first page.
- `include_archived` (argument, boolean, optional) - Compatibility flag retained for callers that request historical rows; public scans never return archived or terminal bodies. Use dedicated terminal-audit surfaces for hash-only audit markers.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Page size (1–1000).
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope filter. When set, only entities with exactly this workspace_hash are returned ("" targets only global entities). Omit for unscoped.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "has_more": {
      "name": "has_more",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when another page exists."
    },
    "items": {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Entities in this page, ordered by id ascending, with expanded body_json fields at top level.",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "next_cursor": {
      "name": "next_cursor",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "Pass this as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Null on the final page."
    },
    "total": {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities in this page."
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_hygiene

Summary: Startup-Memory Hygiene Report

Read-only hygiene report: surface likely low-signal memories so a startup-memory block stays dense without manual forensics. Scores every active memory by startup 'actionability' (the same signal as recall's startup mode) — concrete anchors like issue/ticket keys, #refs, paths, URLs, named systems, and decision/escalation language score high; vague, date-only titles (e.g. '2026-07-13') and very short bodies score low — and returns the worst offenders (below `threshold`) with the reasons they were flagged. Keyset-scans in pages; never bumps retrieval counts or decay. Use it to find archive/consolidate candidates before curating startup recall.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Restrict the scan to one category, e.g. 'memories'. Omit to scan every active category.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum flagged rows to return, worst first (1–1000).
- `scan_limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum active memories to scan (1–10000).
- `threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Actionability score (0.0–1.0) below which a memory is flagged low-signal. Lower = stricter (fewer flags).

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "flagged": {
      "name": "flagged",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Worst-first: {id, category, key, actionability, reasons[], retrieval_count}. reasons ∈ date_only_title | short_body | no_concrete_entities | low_actionability.",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "flagged_count": {
      "name": "flagged_count",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Total memories below the threshold (may exceed the returned rows)."
    },
    "returned": {
      "name": "returned",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of flagged rows in this response."
    },
    "scanned": {
      "name": "scanned",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of active memories inspected."
    },
    "threshold": {
      "name": "threshold",
      "type": "number",
      "description": "The actionability threshold applied."
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_promote

Summary: Promote Memory

Promote a memory across the class ladder (to_category) and/or the scope ladder (to_workspace_hash) per the shared-memory promotion ladder (perseus docs/shared-memory-promotion-ladder.md §4). Creates a new entity that carries a promoted_from provenance record (source category/key/id/scope, reason, timestamp) and links the source to it with relationship='promoted_to'. The source entity is never edited or hidden — raw evidence stays reachable. Uses skip_dedup internally so the promoted copy always creates its own key even when near-identical to the source.

Parameters:
- `from_category` (argument, string, required) - Category of the source entity to promote
- `from_key` (argument, string, required) - Key of the source entity to promote
- `reason` (argument, string, optional) - Why this promotion is happening (recorded in promoted_from).
- `to_category` (argument, string, optional) - Target class/category. Omit to keep the source category.
- `to_key` (argument, string, optional) - Target key. Omit to keep the source key.
- `to_workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Target scope (workspace_hash; empty string = global). Omit to keep the source scope.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "name": "action",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "'created' or 'updated' for the target entity"
    },
    "from_id": {
      "name": "from_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "promoted": {
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_beliefs

Summary: Derived Beliefs Overlay

Derived-belief overlay (#717, spec: docs/specs/belief-overlay.md): compute the current effective belief for a topic from the live entity store, with fresh local corrections always outranking stale global beliefs regardless of semantic similarity (precedence tiers are absolute, never blended).

Parameters:
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum belief candidates to return
- `topic` (argument, string, required) - Topic or question to resolve the current effective belief for
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Optional workspace scope for the local-correction tier

##### TOOL perseus_vault_claim_card

Summary: Evidence-Backed Claim Card

Evidence-backed claim card (#852, spec: docs/specs/claim-cards.md): a deterministic, versioned projection of one entity's claim, provenance class (source_human/fact_extracted/fact_derived/inference_agent), valid vs recorded time, confidence/support, supersession/contradiction/stale state, evidence references, a sanitized agent_projection hash-bound to the selected evidence and policy, and machine-readable reason codes (serveable / archived / scope_mismatch / revoked_access + flags). Read-only view over existing entities and links — never a second source of truth.

Parameters:
- `agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Legacy caller field; public authorization uses the transport-stamped requesting_agent_id.
- `entity_id` (argument, string, required) - ID of the entity to project as a claim card
- `include_agent_projection` (argument, boolean, optional) - Include the sanitized agent_projection block
- `include_evidence` (argument, boolean, optional) - Include evidence references (metadata only; raw bodies never cross)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped requester identity; required at runtime and never trusted from model input.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Caller's workspace scope for visibility enforcement (workspace-scoped entities mismatch → withheld with scope_mismatch)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_ask

Summary: Ask Question from Memories

Ask a natural language question and get a grounded answer from stored memories via RAG. Internally recalls top-k entities, assembles context, and queries the configured LLM (Ollama) for an answer with cited sources. Requires --llm-endpoint to be set. LLM request timeout defaults to 30s; set PERSEUS_VAULT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECS for large/cold models that need longer to load (#528).

Parameters:
- `as_of_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional) - #472 Temporal RAG: answer from the memory context AS IT WAS BELIEVED at this transaction-time instant (unix ms) — the retrieved bodies are reconstructed to the versions live at that instant, so a corrected-later fact does not leak into the past answer. Combine with valid_at_unix_ms for the full bi-temporal cell. Omit for the live view.
- `query` (argument, string, required) - Natural language question to answer from stored memories
- `top_k` (argument, integer, optional) - Number of top entities to use as context (max 20)
- `valid_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional) - #472 Temporal RAG: answer from the context that was TRUE IN THE WORLD at this valid-time instant (unix ms), per current (or as_of) knowledge. Omit for the live view.
- `verify_stale_observations` (argument, boolean, optional) - #884: stale-observation gate. When true (default), observation sources with newer unconsolidated raw facts are verified against those facts before citation — consistent facts are cited with a 'verified against raw facts' note, contradicted observations are refused and reported in refused_sources. Set false to disable the gate.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "answer": {
      "name": "answer",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Grounded answer with cited sources"
    },
    "sources": {
      "name": "sources",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Cited source entities used in the answer",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "category": {
            "name": "category",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "key": {
            "name": "key",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "score": {
            "name": "score",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "snippet": {
            "name": "snippet",
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_history

Summary: perseus_vault_history

List superseded (historical) versions of a fact (category + key), newest first. Each entry was the live fact for an interval before it was overwritten. The companion to perseus_vault_as_of: as_of returns the single version live at one instant; history returns the version trail. Paginated: returns the `limit` newest versions (default 20) starting at `offset`; `total` in the response is the FULL trail size, so total > returned means there are more pages. Returns an empty list if the fact has never been overwritten (its only version is the current live one in recall).

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key within the category
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum versions to return (newest first), 0-1000. Defaults to 20. 0 is count-only: returns no version bodies while `total` still reports the full trail size.
- `offset` (argument, integer, optional) - Number of newest versions to skip, for paging through a long trail.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_as_of

Summary: Time-Travel Entity Lookup

Transaction-time time-travel: return the version of a fact (category + key) that Perseus Vault believed at a given past instant. When a fact is overwritten, the prior version is kept in history; this returns whichever version was live at as_of_unix_ms. Use to answer 'what did we believe about X back then?' or to audit how a fact changed. For the orthogonal valid-time axis ('what was actually TRUE in the world at time T') use perseus_vault_valid_at; for both axes at once use perseus_vault_bitemporal. Returns found=false if the fact had not been recorded yet at that time. If the instant falls inside a window compacted by history retention (#398), returns an explicit marker (compacted=true, versions_compacted, digest) instead of the original — now unrecoverable — versions.

Parameters:
- `as_of_unix_ms` (argument, integer, required) - Transaction-time instant (unix ms) to travel to
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key within the category

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "as_of_unix_ms": {
      "name": "as_of_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "body_json": {
      "name": "body_json",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The fact's content as it was at as_of_unix_ms"
    },
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "compacted": {
      "name": "compacted",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Present and true when the instant falls inside a retention-compacted window: the result is a tombstone marker, not a real version (#398)"
    },
    "digest": {
      "name": "digest",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Hash-chain digest folded over the evicted versions (#398)"
    },
    "entity_type": {
      "name": "entity_type",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "False if the fact had not been recorded by as_of_unix_ms"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "status": {
      "name": "status",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "versions_compacted": {
      "name": "versions_compacted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "How many original versions the compacted window rolled up (#398)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_valid_at

Summary: Valid-Time Lookup (What Was True)

Valid-time (application-time) lookup: return the version of a fact (category + key) that — per CURRENT knowledge — was actually true in the world at a given instant. Orthogonal to perseus_vault_as_of: as_of answers 'what did we BELIEVE at time T' (transaction time); valid_at answers 'what WAS TRUE at time T, as we understand it now'. Facts carry a valid period [valid_from, valid_to) settable on perseus_vault_remember; a later-recorded version's claim supersedes earlier claims for the instants it covers. Returns found=false if no version's valid period contains the instant.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key within the category
- `valid_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, required) - World-instant (unix ms) to evaluate: which version was actually true then

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "body_json": {
      "name": "body_json",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The fact's content as it was true at the instant"
    },
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "entity_type": {
      "name": "entity_type",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "False if no version's valid period contains the instant"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "is_live_version": {
      "name": "is_live_version",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when the matched version is the current live row (not superseded)"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "recorded_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "recorded_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Transaction time the matched version was recorded"
    },
    "status": {
      "name": "status",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "valid_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "valid_from_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_from_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Start of the matched version's valid period"
    },
    "valid_to_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_to_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "End of the matched version's valid period (absent = still true)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_bitemporal

Summary: Bi-Temporal Rectangle Query

Full bi-temporal query (SQL:2011 SYSTEM_TIME + APPLICATION_TIME): 'as of transaction time tx_at, which version did we believe was true in the world at valid time valid_at?' Returns the exact cell of the bi-temporal rectangle — the audit-grade 'who knew what, as-of-when' question. Combines both axes: perseus_vault_as_of is this with valid_at pinned to tx_at; perseus_vault_valid_at is this with tx_at pinned to now. Retroactive and proactive updates land in the correct rectangle cell. Returns found=false if nothing recorded by tx_at was valid at valid_at.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key within the category
- `tx_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, required) - Transaction-time instant (unix ms): reconstruct knowledge as of this moment
- `valid_at_unix_ms` (argument, integer, required) - Valid-time instant (unix ms): the world-moment being asked about

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "body_json": {
      "name": "body_json",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The version occupying that bi-temporal rectangle cell"
    },
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "entity_type": {
      "name": "entity_type",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "False if nothing recorded by tx_at was valid at valid_at"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "invalidated_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "invalidated_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Transaction time this version was retired (absent = live)"
    },
    "is_live_version": {
      "name": "is_live_version",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "recorded_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "recorded_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "status": {
      "name": "status",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "tx_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "tx_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "valid_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "valid_from_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_from_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "valid_to_unix_ms": {
      "name": "valid_to_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_learned_artifact_register

##### TOOL perseus_vault_artifact_manifest

Summary: Serve Artifact Manifest

Serve the compact deterministic manifest for one artifact identity after scope + visibility filtering. When workspace_hash is omitted, only global bindings are considered — an artifact hash alone is a pointer, not an access grant.

Parameters:
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Optional requesting agent id for visibility filtering.
- `sha256` (argument, string, required) - Full 64-hex SHA-256 content identity
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Exact workspace scope to read; omit for global-only.


##### TOOL perseus_vault_embed

Summary: Generate Entity Embeddings

Generate and store dense vector embeddings for entities via Ollama /api/embed. Supports single entity (category+key) or batch mode (batch_category). Requires --llm-endpoint to be set. #885: also the operator surface for optional quantized embedding storage — quant_mode converts ALL stored float32 embeddings to int8 or bit (MIB-style sign-bit vectors scored by Hamming) in one transaction with a pre-quantization snapshot; restore_quantized_backup rolls back losslessly from that snapshot; drop_quantized_backup removes it after verification.

Parameters:
- `batch_category` (argument, string, optional) - Embed all entities in this category lacking embeddings
- `batch_limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max entities in batch mode
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Entity category for single mode
- `drop_quantized_backup` (argument, boolean, optional) - Drop the pre-quantization snapshot after verifying the quantized store (irreversible; rollback then requires re-embed)
- `key` (argument, string, optional) - Entity key for single mode
- `quant_mode` (argument, string, optional) - Store-wide reindex: convert ALL stored embeddings from float32 to int8 or bit (one transaction; pre-quantization float32 snapshot created once). Refused when already quantized — restore first.
- `restore_quantized_backup` (argument, boolean, optional) - Roll back the embedding column to float32 from the pre-quantization snapshot (lossless for rows that existed at quantization time)
- `text` (argument, string, optional) - Text to embed (omit to use entity body_json)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "dimensions": {
      "name": "dimensions",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Vector dimensions"
    },
    "embedded": {
      "name": "embedded",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities embedded"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_prune

Summary: Prune Stale Entities

Bulk archive entities by category, decay threshold, or age. Use dry_run=true to preview without archiving. Useful for cleaning stale or low-quality memories. With scope='history' (#398) it instead evicts old superseded versions from entity_history under the given (or env-configured PERSEUS_VAULT_HISTORY_*) bounds, rolling each evicted run into a compaction tombstone; dry_run reports the rows and bytes that would be evicted.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Archive entities in this category
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Preview without archiving/evicting
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max entities to prune (0 = unlimited)
- `max_age_days` (argument, integer, optional) - scope='history': evict versions invalidated more than this many days ago (overrides PERSEUS_VAULT_HISTORY_MAX_AGE_DAYS)
- `max_bytes` (argument, integer, optional) - scope='history': global stored-history byte budget, globally-oldest evicted first (overrides PERSEUS_VAULT_HISTORY_MAX_BYTES)
- `max_versions_per_key` (argument, integer, optional) - scope='history': keep at most this many stored versions per key, oldest evicted first (overrides PERSEUS_VAULT_HISTORY_MAX_VERSIONS_PER_KEY)
- `min_decay` (argument, number, optional) - Archive entities with decay_score below this threshold
- `older_than_days` (argument, integer, optional) - Archive entities older than this many days
- `scope` (argument, string, optional) - 'history' prunes superseded versions from entity_history under retention bounds instead of archiving live entities (#398)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "archived": {
      "name": "archived",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "examined": {
      "name": "examined",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "reason": {
      "name": "reason",
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_journal

Summary: Append Journal Entry

Append a structured decision/observation log entry. Uses evaluated/acted/forward pattern: what was considered, what was done, and what happens next. Essential for audit trails and timeline reconstruction. Public admission_source events additionally require an initialized clientInfo.name and an enforce-mode memory.admission.source authority for the exact workspace; caller-supplied identities are never authoritative.

Parameters:
- `acted` (argument, object, optional) - What action was taken and why
- `agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Agent identity (v1.2.0). Records which agent created this journal event.
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Related entity category for linking
- `entity_id` (argument, string, optional) - Related entity ID for linking
- `evaluated` (argument, object, optional) - What was evaluated: options considered, context, constraints
- `event_type` (argument, string, optional) - Event type: 'decision', 'observation', 'action', 'error'
- `forward` (argument, object, optional) - What the plan is going forward
- `key` (argument, string, optional) - Related entity key for linking
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped caller identity; required for admission_source events.
- `source_attestation` (argument, string, optional) - HMAC-SHA256 attestation over the canonical admission-source fields; required for public admission_source events and never stored.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Explicit workspace attribution for the journal event; empty string denotes the global partition.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "created_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "created_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Creation timestamp in unix milliseconds"
    },
    "event_type": {
      "name": "event_type",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Event type recorded"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Journal event ID"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_check_failure_pattern

Summary: Check Failure Pattern (Deja-Vu Guard)

Deja-vu guard (#521): call BEFORE retrying a failed command or committing to an approach. Checks the action against workspace-scoped prior failures in both the journal (error events and failure-marked acted/forward payloads) and the entity store (failure/pitfall/root-cause memories), ranked by similarity, recency, and trust. Returns matching prior failures with the recorded cause and resolution, a deja_vu flag, and a one-line warning when the action was already tried and failed. Read-only: never bumps retrieval counts or decay. Record failures via perseus_vault_journal (event_type 'error') or perseus_vault_remember so the guard can find them.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, required) - The command line or approach description you are about to (re)try, e.g. 'cargo build --no-default-features' or 'parse the changelog with a regex'
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum number of matches to return (1-50)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, required) - Required workspace scope. Use an empty string only for the explicit global partition; other workspaces are never searched.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "deja_vu": {
      "name": "deja_vu",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when at least one prior recorded failure matches the action"
    },
    "matches": {
      "name": "matches",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Prior failures matching the action, best first. Each includes source, ref, workspace_hash, when (unix ms), what_failed, cause, resolution, and score.",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "workspace_hash": {
            "name": "workspace_hash",
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Stored workspace scope of the matched failure; empty means the global partition."
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "message": {
      "name": "message",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Unambiguous empty state ('no prior failures recorded matching this action') when nothing matches"
    },
    "warning": {
      "name": "warning",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "One-line agent-actionable deja-vu warning (present only when matches exist)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_health

Summary: Check Health

Cheap readiness probe for the vault server and its SQLite database. Returns healthy/unhealthy plus a readiness snapshot: `ready` (DB answers AND at least one active memory), `active_memories`, `embedded_memories`, `semantic_recall` (available|no_coverage|disabled), `db_path`, and `warnings[]` with likely causes. Call this before a recall-heavy workflow, or when recall unexpectedly returns empty, to tell an empty/degraded store apart from a broken MCP child. Use perseus_vault_stats for detailed statistics.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "active_memories": {
      "name": "active_memories",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Count of non-archived memories (the set recall reads)"
    },
    "binary_path": {
      "name": "binary_path",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Absolute path of the running binary (empty when undeterminable)"
    },
    "binary_stale": {
      "name": "binary_stale",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when the running binary was replaced on disk since this process started (#858): results come from a stale image — call perseus_vault_handoff_restart or restart the session"
    },
    "db_path": {
      "name": "db_path",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Absolute path of the SQLite file this server is bound to (#671)"
    },
    "embedded_memories": {
      "name": "embedded_memories",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Count of active memories carrying a dense embedding"
    },
    "pid": {
      "name": "pid",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "PID of the running server process"
    },
    "ready": {
      "name": "ready",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when the DB responds AND the store has at least one active memory — i.e. recall can return non-empty results"
    },
    "semantic_recall": {
      "name": "semantic_recall",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Dense/hybrid posture: available (backend on, coverage present), no_coverage (backend on, nothing embedded), or disabled (keyword-only build/config)",
      "enum": [
        "available",
        "no_coverage",
        "disabled"
      ]
    },
    "status": {
      "name": "status",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Server health status (healthy iff the DB responds)",
      "enum": [
        "healthy",
        "unhealthy"
      ]
    },
    "warnings": {
      "name": "warnings",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Likely-cause messages for degraded/empty states; empty when nominal",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_deployment_profile

Summary: Deployment Profile

Resolved runtime deployment profile (#870): one machine-readable answer to 'what is this vault actually connected to?'. Reports the profile class (`offline` | `local_only` | `local_with_approved_network` | `external_actions_enabled`), model backend (bundled/ollama/provider/none), embedding backend (kind + available + degraded — a missing/unavailable local backend is reported as degraded, never silently reclassified as empty success), network listeners and non-loopback egress hosts (hosts only — sanitized, no URLs/keys/raw bodies), connectors, cloud-provider use, external-mutation posture, encryption at rest (aes_256_gcm|plaintext + storage-state probe) and in transit, and raw-retention policy. Describes ACTUAL runtime state: offline mode zeroes web/LLM/embedding/connectors at startup, and the profile reflects the effective flags. Read-only.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "cloud_provider_use": {
      "name": "cloud_provider_use",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "'none' or comma-joined non-loopback hosts"
    },
    "connectors": {
      "name": "connectors",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "name/remote/remote_host"
    },
    "embedding_backend": {
      "name": "embedding_backend",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "kind/available/degraded/semantic_recall"
    },
    "encryption": {
      "name": "encryption",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "at_rest/storage_state/in_transit"
    },
    "external_mutations": {
      "name": "external_mutations",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "disabled",
        "enabled"
      ]
    },
    "model_backend": {
      "name": "model_backend",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "kind/model/available/degraded"
    },
    "network": {
      "name": "network",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "listeners/egress_hosts/loopback_only"
    },
    "profile": {
      "name": "profile",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Derived deployment class from runtime state",
      "enum": [
        "offline",
        "local_only",
        "local_with_approved_network",
        "external_actions_enabled"
      ]
    },
    "raw_retention": {
      "name": "raw_retention",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "memory_bodies/raw_logs"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_config_report

Summary: Config Self-Report

Per-stage provider/config self-report with a requested-vs-resolved diff (#1010). One machine-readable answer to 'did every pipeline stage actually resolve the configuration I asked for?' Reports six stages — embedding_backend, model_backend, quantization, db_path, encryption, network — each with `requested` (the operator-facing knob as literally given, sanitized: hosts/kind labels only, never secrets), `resolved` (the runtime's actual resolution), `drifted` (true when they differ in a way the operator did not ask for), and `note` (remediation). Drift is a loud condition: a configured-but-unavailable embedding backend is reported as drifted, never silently reclassified as empty success; a store whose embedding format was declared by a previous process drifts against this process's default. Read-only.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "drifted_stages": {
      "name": "drifted_stages",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Stage ids with drifted=true (empty = everything resolved as requested)"
    },
    "generated_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "generated_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Report timestamp"
    },
    "stages": {
      "name": "stages",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "One entry per stage: stage/requested/resolved/drifted/note"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_type_policies

Summary: Typed Memory Policies

Typed memory-class policy table (#1000, CogniCore borrow): the 8 MemoryTypes (semantic, episodic, procedural, preference, constraint, failure, reflection, knowledge) with per-type decay_multiplier (scales the per-category half-life at decay tick) and retrieval_weight (multiplies the final fused recall score), plus each policy's rationale. Legacy rows (memory_type '') resolve to the SEMANTIC policy — the byte-compatible baseline. Unknown memory_type values on remember() are hard write errors (fail-closed, never a silent fallback). Read-only.

```json
      "description": "Write-time validation semantics"
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_handoff_restart

Summary: perseus_vault_handoff_restart

Live-update / reconnect for long-lived stdio sessions (#858). When the perseus-vault binary was rebuilt or replaced on disk mid-session, the running process image is stale: every other tool refuses loudly (isError) until the session is restarted — or this tool hot-swaps the process on the SAME stdio connection. States: binary unchanged -> no_handoff_needed (identity report); stale + dry_run -> dry_run (what would happen); stale without confirm -> confirm_required; stale + confirm:true -> the replacement binary is spawned on this session's stdio and the old process exits immediately after this response — the MCP session continues uninterrupted in the new process image. Do not pipeline requests during the handoff.

Parameters:
- `confirm` (argument, boolean, optional) - Required to actually perform the hot-swap when the binary is stale (default false)
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Report what would happen without performing the handoff (default false)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_quality_telemetry

Machine-readable memory-quality telemetry: contradiction rate, supersession lag, class/layer distribution, and promotion-flow proxy.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Category for contradiction scan (default general).

##### TOOL perseus_vault_retrieval_telemetry

Summary: perseus_vault_retrieval_telemetry

Read-only retrieval telemetry: concentration (top slot/token shares, Herfindahl), repeated-serving rate over a turn/second window, diversity (sources, source classes, Simpson), cross-arm contamination (per-arm audits, delivered-set validation, optional arm-level probe), low-trust query-class fan-out, and diversity/cooldown displacement. Reports include denominators, scope, retrieval profile, source class, and the versioned artifact hash; empty/degraded/unavailable states are separated from zero concentration.

Parameters:
- `probe_mode` (argument, string, optional) - Probe mode: lexical|dense|hybrid|fused|graph|proactive (default lexical).
- `probe_query` (argument, string, optional) - Optional contamination probe: run arm-level SQL deltas for this query and report blocked re-entry per arm.
- `profile` (argument, string, optional) - Scope: only events recorded under this profile.
- `window_secs` (argument, integer, optional) - Window in seconds (default 86400).
- `window_turns` (argument, integer, optional) - Window in serving batches (distinct recalls). Default: none (window_secs wins).
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Scope: only events from this workspace.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_purge

Summary: Purge Archived Entities

Permanently delete all archived entities and run VACUUM to reclaim disk space. This is the only operation that actually removes entities — prune/forget only soft-archive. Erasure is complete (#398): every superseded version of a purged entity is deleted from entity_history, and journal rows referencing it are redacted in place (payloads scrubbed; rows kept so the audit hash chain stays verifiable). Purged data is DELETED and NOT RECOVERABLE — this forget-then-purge path is the GDPR-style erasure mechanism. Supports dry_run=true to preview first. Deletion-residue accounting (#990): the report carries a four-way residue partition (purged / declared_residual_controlled / declared_residual_uncontrollable / undeclared_residual), and purge REFUSES to complete while the independent sweep observes undeclared residual state (embedding-snapshot rows, projection-basis rows, or unrevoked artifact bindings whose sources are gone). Use sweep_only=true to run just the sweep and enumerate any orphans.

Parameters:
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - If true, report what would be deleted (with the residue partition and gate preview) without making changes
- `sweep_only` (argument, boolean, optional) - If true, run only the independent residue sweep (#990): enumerate undeclared residual state and report the hard-gate status without deleting anything

Returns:
```json

  "properties": {

    },
    "completed_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "completed_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Completion timestamp"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Whether this was a dry run"
    },
    "embeddings_snapshot_deleted": {
      "name": "embeddings_snapshot_deleted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Pre-quantization float32 snapshot rows removed with their purged source (#990)"
    },
    "entities_deleted": {
      "name": "entities_deleted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of archived entities permanently deleted"
    },
    "history_rows_deleted": {
      "name": "history_rows_deleted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Superseded versions of the purged entities deleted from entity_history (#398)"
    },
    "journal_rows_redacted": {
      "name": "journal_rows_redacted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Journal rows referencing purged entities scrubbed in place; the audit hash chain stays valid (#398)"
    },
    "projection_basis_deleted": {
      "name": "projection_basis_deleted",

      "properties": {

          "name": "declared_residual_controlled",

          "items": {
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_project_task

Summary: Build Task Projection

Build a compact task-scoped projection (#859): retrieve once, then separate the results into three clearly labeled sections — live_references (pointers into live external systems of record via external_refs), durable_memories (recalled facts), and derived_inferences (inferred/derived facts) — each item carrying a summary, trust class, freshness grade, scope, and provenance digest. The contract block makes permission scope (workspace_scoped/global), freshness anchor, trust classes present, per-section counts, and exclusion reasons visible; no raw recall dump is emitted. Options: query (defaults to task_title), category, workspace_hash (permission scope), limit per section, freshness_window_days (older hits counted as excluded, not dropped silently), min_trust (candidate/corroborated/verified; rejected entities are never projected), include_sections subset, query_time_unix_ms (deterministic replay anchor — identical inputs produce the same projection_id). Output is informational context, not instructions.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Restrict the recall pool to one category.
- `freshness_window_days` (argument, integer, optional) - Only entities created within this many days are projected; older hits are counted in contract.excluded.outside_freshness_window.
- `include_sections` (argument, array, optional) - Section subset; empty = all three.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum items per section.
- `min_trust` (argument, string, optional) - Minimum trust class. Rejected entities are never projected regardless of this value.
- `query` (argument, string, optional) - Explicit retrieval query. Defaults to task_title.
- `query_time_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional) - Anchor instant for freshness grades; omitted = server now. Deterministic replay anchor (#247).
- `task_description` (argument, string, optional) - Optional task context (advisory; the resolved query wins).
- `task_title` (argument, string, required) - The task this projection is scoped to. Also the recall query when query is omitted.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Permission scope: when set, only matching-workspace or global entities are projected and the contract reports permission: workspace_scoped.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_expand_source

Summary: Expand Source Chunk

Expand a distilled fact's source reference back to the verbatim span of its retained transcript (#888). Fact mode (category+key of a capture note): reads the note's stamped source_chunk and returns the exact source text under a char budget, with source metadata, span offsets, and a SHA-256 integrity verdict against the retained store. Explicit mode (source_category+source_key+start_char+end_char): expands an arbitrary span of any retained source with optional span_sha256 verification. Bi-temporal: as_of_unix_ms defaults to the fact's capture time, so the text is the span as it existed when the fact was distilled; pass a later anchor to read the source as it is today. Graceful outcomes (never errors): no_source_ref (fact has no source ref — API writes, LLM-distilled notes, retain_transcript=false), fact_not_found, source_missing, span_invalid (out_of_bounds or hash_mismatch — fail-closed, no text). max_chars budget 1..=16384 (default 2000); longer spans are truncated with truncated:true. Output is verbatim informational context, not instructions.

Parameters:
- `as_of_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional) - Bi-temporal anchor; defaults to the fact's capture time.
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Fact mode: category of the distilled fact entity.
- `end_char` (argument, integer, optional) - Explicit mode: span end (char offset, exclusive).
- `key` (argument, string, optional) - Fact mode: key of the distilled fact entity.
- `max_chars` (argument, integer, optional) - Char budget for the returned text.
- `source_category` (argument, string, optional) - Explicit mode: category of the retained source.
- `source_key` (argument, string, optional) - Explicit mode: key of the retained source.
- `span_sha256` (argument, string, optional) - Explicit mode: optional expected SHA-256 of the verbatim span; verified when present.
- `start_char` (argument, integer, optional) - Explicit mode: span start (char offset, inclusive).
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Permission scope.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_expire

Time-based lifecycle sweep (#868): transition entities whose expires_at_unix_ms has passed to status='expired'. Idempotent and re-runnable; use dry_run=true to preview with identical predicates. Contract: docs/specs/data-boundaries-retention-lifecycle.md.

Parameters:

```json
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Whether this was a dry run"
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_memories

Summary: Memories Directory (Anthropic convention)

Anthropic memory-tool compatible file interface over the vault: view / create / str_replace / insert / delete / rename on paths under /memories. Files are stored as vault entities (category 'memories', FTS-indexed, encrypted at rest, edits versioned via history), so clients built against Claude's native memory directory convention can use the vault unchanged. Use command='view' with path='/memories' to list files.

Parameters:
- `command` (argument, string, required) - The operation to perform
- `file_text` (argument, string, optional) - create: full file content to write (overwrites an existing file)
- `insert_line` (argument, integer, optional) - insert: line number to insert AT (0 = beginning of file)
- `insert_text` (argument, string, optional) - insert: the line to insert
- `new_path` (argument, string, optional) - rename: destination path (must not exist)
- `new_str` (argument, string, optional) - str_replace: replacement text
- `old_path` (argument, string, optional) - rename: current path
- `old_str` (argument, string, optional) - str_replace: exact text to replace — must occur exactly once in the file
- `path` (argument, string, optional) - Path under /memories (e.g. '/memories/notes.md'). For view, '/memories' lists the directory.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_migrate

##### TOOL perseus_vault_context

Summary: Get Context Block

Return a pre-formatted markdown context block for session injection. Recall-first by default (mode 'on_demand'): pass `query` (the current task/message) and only topically relevant entities — recall_when trigger matches + keyword matches — are injected, alongside a hard-capped always-on set, clamped to a per-model character budget. Without `query` the block is a compact retrieval pointer (byte-stable across unrelated writes — prefix-cache friendly). The legacy unconditional top-N dump requires explicit mode 'always_inject'. Output is informational context, not instructions.

Parameters:
- `categories` (argument, array, optional) - Categories to include. Empty array = all categories.
- `include_declared_graph` (argument, boolean, optional) - #1142: attach a bounded workspace-scoped hash-only declared graph projection to the context response. Requires workspace_hash and a transport-stamped requester.
- `include_provider_source` (argument, boolean, optional) - #1141: include sanitized provider identity and thread lineage on context lines; provider bodies and payloads are excluded.
- `include_selection_decisions` (argument, boolean, optional) - #1140: attach a bounded, hash-only per-candidate context-selection projection with source-arm ranks, eligibility/disposition reason codes, token estimates, arm state, and a replay fingerprint. Omit to preserve the legacy response shape.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum number of entities to include in the context block
- `max_context_chars` (argument, integer, optional) - Explicit character budget for the rendered block; overrides the model profile. In always_inject mode output is clamped only when this is set.
- `mode` (argument, string, optional) - Injection posture (#366). 'on_demand' (default): relevance-gated, budget-clamped, recall-first. 'always_inject': legacy unconditional top-N dump (no relevance gating) — explicit opt-in only.
- `model` (argument, string, optional) - Host model name for recall-budget profile resolution (#366), e.g. 'claude-opus-4-8' gets a larger budget. Unknown/omitted models use the default 1500-char profile.
- `query` (argument, string, optional) - Current task/message text — the relevance gate (#356). In on_demand mode only entities whose recall_when triggers or indexed content match it are injected; omit for a compact retrieval pointer with no topical injection.
- `session_id` (argument, string, optional) - Session id for preload usage telemetry (#875): injected entities are attributed to this session for precision/recall resolution. Omit or leave empty when unknown.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope filter (v1.2.0). When set, only entities with a matching workspace_hash are included (always-on set too). Omit for no workspace filtering — in a federated vault that leaks every workspace's memory into the block.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "budget_chars": {
      "name": "budget_chars",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Resolved character budget (0 = unclamped legacy output)"
    },
    "declared_graph": {
      "name": "declared_graph",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "#1142: optional bounded declared graph projection with hash-only source, span, scope, origin, validity, and support state."
    },
    "entities_injected": {
      "name": "entities_injected",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities actually injected (always-on + topical)"
    },
    "markdown": {
      "name": "markdown",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Markdown-formatted context block with entity details"
    },
    "mode": {
      "name": "mode",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Resolved injection mode: on_demand or always_inject"
    },
    "selection_decisions": {
      "name": "selection_decisions",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "#1140: optional bounded, hash-only context-selection projection. Contains policy/schema digests, candidate/retention counts, arm states, token estimates, dispositions, delivered order, and replay fingerprint; it never contains query text or memory bodies."
    },
    "total_chars": {
      "name": "total_chars",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Character count of the markdown content"
    },
    "warnings": {
      "name": "warnings",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Soft warnings: always-on cap overflow, budget truncation",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_capture

Summary: Capture Session Insights

Opt-in in-session memory capture (#520): distill a session transcript or insight payload into durable memory entities the moment a problem is solved, instead of waiting for a scheduled harvest. Splits the payload into candidate notes (headed sections, paragraphs, or JSONL records — auto-detected), classifies each by cheap local signals into root-cause / pitfall / decision / pattern / takeaway, and writes each through the normal remember path with source='capture' (layer buffer, moderate importance). Fully local and deterministic by default — no LLM, no network; pass llm=true to distill via the configured --llm-endpoint instead (falls back to the rule-based path on any LLM failure or timeout). Anti-flood by design: near-duplicate merging stays ON (a re-captured solved problem merges into the existing memory), same-headline notes update in place, and writes are capped per invocation with dropped notes reported. Nothing runs automatically — capture happens only when this tool (or the `perseus-vault capture` CLI verb) is explicitly invoked, e.g. from an on_insight or SessionEnd lifecycle hook (run `maintain` after end-of-session capture).

Request body: application/json

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "candidates": {
      "name": "candidates",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Candidate notes found in the payload before capping"
    },
    "captured": {
      "name": "captured",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of notes distilled (and written, unless dry_run)"
    },
    "consumed": {
      "name": "consumed",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "#563: number of captured regions removed from source_file (0 unless consume=true and the prune ran). See source_backup / consume_skipped / consume_error."
    },
    "created": {
      "name": "created",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Notes that created a new entity"
    },
    "distiller": {
      "name": "distiller",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "'rule_based' or 'llm' — which distiller produced the notes"
    },
    "dropped": {
      "name": "dropped",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Candidate notes dropped by the per-invocation cap"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "True when nothing was written"
    },
    "llm_fallback": {
      "name": "llm_fallback",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Present when llm=true was requested but the rule-based path was used; says why"
    },
    "merged": {
      "name": "merged",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Notes merged into an existing near-duplicate entity by the trigram dedup (the capture flood control)"
    },
    "message": {
      "name": "message",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Unambiguous empty state when the payload contained nothing durable"
    },
    "notes": {
      "name": "notes",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Per-note report: {id, key, type, summary, action}",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "source_backup": {
      "name": "source_backup",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "#563: path to the pre-prune backup (<source_file>.bak) written when consumed > 0"
    },
    "updated": {
      "name": "updated",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Notes that updated an existing entity in place (same category+key)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_score

Summary: Score Entity Quality

Assign a quality score (0.0–1.0) to an entity. The score persists as an importance floor: decay_tick/cohere never recompute decay_score below it, so an explicitly scored memory survives idle time indefinitely (fidelity beats recency). Scores >= 0.7 also mark the entity verified. Re-score with 0.0 to clear the floor. Use this to mark entities as accurate, verified, or deprecated.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category to score
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key to score
- `score` (argument, number, required) - Quality score 0.0–1.0. 1.0 = verified, 0.5 = neutral, 0.0 = low quality

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entity category"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Whether the entity was found"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Entity key"
    },
    "score": {
      "name": "score",
      "type": "number",
      "description": "Quality score assigned"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_follow

Summary: Record Follow/Miss Efficacy Signal

Record whether an entity (typically a convention/insight/lesson) was actually FOLLOWED or MISSED by the agent — the honest follow-rate signal. Unlike retrieval_count (how often a memory is recalled), this tracks whether recall changed behavior. After enough attempts, efficacy_status flips to 'useful' or 'dead' and feeds into decay scoring so ignored rules decay out of recall while followed ones resist decay.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Entity category
- `context` (argument, string, optional) - Optional description of the action/context this observation relates to
- `followed` (argument, boolean, required) - true if the agent's action followed/honored this entity's guidance, false if it was ignored/missed
- `key` (argument, string, required) - Entity key
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope filter. When set, the stamped row is resolved with strict workspace equality — the same semantics as a workspace-scoped recall — so the signal lands on the row the agent actually saw (no global fallback). Omit to keep the unscoped deterministic pick (global '' row first, then lexicographically-first workspace).

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "efficacy_status": {
      "name": "efficacy_status",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "'unverified' | 'useful' | 'dead'"
    },
    "follow_count": {
      "name": "follow_count",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "follow_rate": {
      "name": "follow_rate",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Whether the entity was found"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "miss_count": {
      "name": "miss_count",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  }
}
```

Both transitions are hash-only in the response, record an admission_review_started intent before mutation, and append a completed admission_approved/admission_rejected receipt only after durable transition. Public calls require an initialized clientInfo.name and an enforce-mode memory.admission.review authority for the exact workspace.
