##### TOOL perseus_vault_admission_quarantine

Summary: perseus_vault_admission_quarantine

#1026: review the admission-quarantine hold — candidates disposed as `quarantined` by trust admission are sealed OUTSIDE the authoritative head (never served by any read surface; storage presence confers no authority). list (default): active candidates with attempt metadata (no bodies); show: full sealed record incl. decrypted body + admission attempt linkage + hash-only receipt; retire: record the review decision (the row is retained so its proposal identifier stays retired); purge: reclaim retired rows and/or active rows past the age watermark (purged proposal identifiers become reusable). Every decision is journaled (admission_quarantined / admission_quarantine_retired / admission_quarantine_purged). Pending items also surface in perseus_vault_operator_review.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, optional) - list (default) | show | retire | purge
- `id` (argument, string, optional) - Quarantine id (required for show/retire)
- `include_retired` (argument, boolean, optional) - list: include retired rows (default active only)
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional)
- `max_age_days` (argument, integer, optional) - purge: reclaim active rows older than this many days (default 30)
- `purge_retired` (argument, boolean, optional) - purge: reclaim retired rows (default true)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Reviewer identity stamped into the journal (default empty)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope for list (default all)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_writer_handoff

Summary: perseus_vault_writer_handoff

#1027: epoch-fenced writer handoff — prevent split-brain on concurrent multi-agent writes. Directory-serialized lifecycle actions, each appending a signed lifecycle result (receipt digest): prepare (open the handoff pointer; the source may still advance), abort (clear the pointer; source stays active), fence (clear the writer + advance the epoch — after this NO writer is authorized; a crash in the Fence→Activate gap leaves zero writers, fail-closed), retarget (advance target + epoch; the abandoned target can no longer activate), activate (admission against the exact fenced revision; the current target becomes the active writer, epoch advances again). status: read the directory. Every write (remember) against an active directory must present the current writer_epoch — stale writes fail with a stable StaleRevision / WriterEpoch reason. Workspace-scoped; absent directory = unfenced legacy posture.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, optional) - status (default) | prepare | abort | fence | retarget | activate
- `presented_epoch` (argument, integer, optional) - activate: the fenced epoch the activating agent must present (exact match required)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Acting identity — activate requires it to equal target_agent_id; stamped into lifecycle receipts
- `target_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Handoff target agent (required for prepare/retarget)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace whose writer directory is managed (required except status; must be non-empty)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "directory": {
      "name": "directory",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "epoch": {
      "name": "epoch",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "lifecycle_len": {
      "name": "lifecycle_len",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "pointer_state": {
      "name": "pointer_state",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "receipt_digest": {
      "name": "receipt_digest",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "target_agent_id": {
      "name": "target_agent_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "writer_agent_id": {
      "name": "writer_agent_id",
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}

Lists dependent entities ordered by authority (importance) + recency, flags PENDING actions whose cited justification changed (AAR review flag — re-validate freshness before execution), and lists COMPLETED actions for review (external effects are irreversible — flag only, never automatic reversal). Bounded closure: depth_cap (1..16, default 3), age_cap_days (default 365); as_of_unix_ms computes the report at a past transaction instant (v1 filters by dependent creation time; full bi-temporal closure via entity_history is a documented follow-on). Deterministic, zero LLM: identical digest → ok; exists-but-changed → GROUNDING_DRIFT; reconcile score (0.7×minhashJaccard + 0.3×neighborOverlap, HI 0.85 / LO 0.55) → MOVED (auto-rewrite anchor + migrate baseline with a provenance trail) / GONE (flag for review) / AMBIGUOUS (surface candidates for operator review).

##### TOOL perseus_vault_restore_forward

Summary: perseus_vault_restore_forward

#1028: forward-only restoration — restore from a checkpoint directory as an audited VERSION ADVANCE of the current head, never as a rewrite. Each checkpoint entity advances its (category, key, workspace) identity: the pre-restore version moves to entity_history (the parent; a rollback is just another forward migration) and the checkpoint body becomes the new head. Protected authority paths always take CURRENT values — authority, policy, revocation, issuer, writer, epoch, dirSeq/lifecycle, createdFrom/provenance are excluded from the mask (M ∩ P = ∅; only `entities` is maskable in v1), so a restore can never revive a stale credential, resurrect a superseded authority, or undo a recorded external effect (authorized actions untouched). Workspace-scoped; an active writer directory (#1027) requires the current writer_epoch. Report: restored / superseded_current_heads / created / errors.

Parameters:
- `checkpoint_dir` (argument, string, optional) - Directory of vault-format .md files (the vault_export wire shape)
- `path_mask` (argument, array, optional) - State paths to restore (only `entities` in v1; protected paths are refused fail-closed)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Acting identity stamped into the journal
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace to restore into (required)
- `writer_epoch` (argument, integer, optional) - Required when the workspace has an active writer directory (#1027)

Returns:

##### TOOL perseus_vault_op_run

Summary: perseus_vault_op_run

#871: durable long-running operation states. Lifecycle tool for the shared run/run-item contract (maintenance, embed, consolidation, export/import, reindex). Actions: begin (queued; requires op_type, optional scope/input_digest/max_retries 0..10/created_by), start (queued->running), progress (done/failed/total counters; partial derived), complete (running->completed with receipt linkage), fail (running->failed; error_detail is sanitized at rest — secrets masked, length capped), failed_to_start (queued->failed_to_start), cancel (queued|running->cancelled), timeout (running->failed with timeout flag), item_add/item_start/item_complete/item_fail/item_cancel (per-item receipts; UNIQUE(run_id, item_ref)). Terminal states accept no further transitions. Restart recovery marks in-flight runs interrupted (mark-only); resume only via perseus_vault_op_run_retry.

- `done` (argument, integer, optional) - progress: items completed
- `error_class` (argument, string, optional) - fail/item_fail: error class
- `error_detail` (argument, string, optional) - fail/item_fail: detail (sanitized at rest)
- `failed` (argument, integer, optional) - progress: items failed

- `max_retries` (argument, integer, optional)
- `op_type` (argument, string, optional) - Operation kind for begin: consolidate|embed_flush|export|import|decay|maintain|reindex|cohere|compact|custom
- `receipt` (argument, string, optional) - complete: terminal receipt linkage (journal event id / artifact ref)
- `receipt_ref` (argument, string, optional) - item_complete: per-item receipt linkage
- `run_id` (argument, string, optional) - Run id (opr-...) for all actions except begin
- `scope` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace hash or empty for global
- `total` (argument, integer, optional) - progress: expected items (omit to keep stored total)

##### TOOL perseus_vault_preload_review

Summary: perseus_vault_preload_review

#875: operator review queue for preload trigger tuning — the ONLY mutation surface. 'approve' applies the proposal through the audited remember path (journal preload_tuning_applied + entity_history provenance, revision bump): retire removes the trigger from the entity's recall_when (others untouched); add_trigger appends the proposed word. 'dismiss' records the decision without mutating anything. Both are journaled with the operator id.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, optional) - 'list': pending proposals with rationale; 'approve': apply proposal_id; 'dismiss': decline proposal_id with a reason.

- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max proposals for list (1-1000)
- `proposal_id` (argument, string, optional) - Proposal id (required for approve/dismiss)
- `reason` (argument, string, optional) - Dismissal reason (dismiss only)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object"
}

Idempotent: re-seeding updates in place, never duplicates. Advisory metadata only — never gates writes.

- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope for the guide entity (empty = global).

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "name": "action",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "key": {
      "name": "key",
      "type": "string"
    }
  }

##### TOOL perseus_vault_declared_schema_set

Summary: Declare Category Retrieval Contract

#923: declare (or replace) the typed retrieval contract for a category — the deterministic exact-match arm. Fields are typed ('scalar' = exact string equality, 'string_list' = array membership) and may be facet-eligible. Advisory retrieval metadata only: never gates writes. Fail-closed validation: unknown field types, duplicate/empty names, reserved names (id/category/key/recall_when/origin/external_refs/expires_at), >32 fields, >16 facets, or >500-byte query_guidance are errors. Re-declaring bumps the schema version; exact-match queries then follow the new contract.

Request body: application/json

Returns:

      "name": "fields",
      "type": "array"
    },
    "ok": {
      "name": "ok",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "query_guidance": {
      "name": "query_guidance",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "version": {
      "name": "version",
      "type": "integer"

##### TOOL perseus_vault_declared_query

Summary: Declared Exact-Match Query

#923: deterministic exact-match retrieval over a declared category — the no-ranking arm. Filters are AND-combined exact-equality checks against the category's declared schema: scalar fields match by exact string equality, string_list fields by array membership. Results come back in deterministic order (created_at ASC, id ASC). Facet counts are truthful and bounded (top 50 distinct values per facet, remainder rolled into 'other'). Fail-closed: undeclared categories, unknown fields, malformed filters, or non-facet facet requests are errors — never degraded to fuzzy recall.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Category with a declared schema (perseus_vault_declared_schema_set)
- `facets` (argument, array, optional) - Facet-eligible fields to count (top 50 distinct values + 'other' bucket)
- `filters` (argument, object, optional) - Exact-equality filters (AND-combined). Scalar field: string value to equal. String-list field: array of strings, any of which must be present.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional)
- `offset` (argument, integer, optional)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Transport-stamped requester identity used for item and facet visibility enforcement.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "facet_counts": {
      "name": "facet_counts",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "items": {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "array"
    },
    "ok": {
      "name": "ok",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "schema": {
      "name": "schema",
      "type": "object"
    },
    "total_matches": {
      "name": "total_matches",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "truncated": {
      "name": "truncated",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  }
}

##### TOOL perseus_vault_conflicts

Summary: Detect Conflicting Entities

Detect conflicting entities in the same category — pairs with low trigram similarity in their body_json. Flags potential contradictions, duplicate-but-divergent entries, and stale-overwritten facts. Read-only by default. Opt in with resolve=true to actively invalidate the lower-certainty side of clear conflicts (superseding it into history, reversible + time-travelable via perseus_vault_as_of); that path defaults to dry_run=true so you preview first, and never resolves pairs whose certainties are within certainty_margin.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Category to scan for conflicts
- `certainty_margin` (argument, number, optional) - Minimum certainty gap to auto-resolve; closer pairs are skipped as ambiguous
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - When resolve=true, only report what would be invalidated unless set false
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum number of conflicts to return / resolve
- `offset` (argument, integer, optional) - Number of entities to skip for pagination
- `resolve` (argument, boolean, optional) - Opt-in: invalidate the lower-certainty side of clear conflicts instead of only reporting them
- `threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Similarity threshold — pairs below this are flagged as conflicts

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "conflicts": {
      "name": "conflicts",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Conflict pairs with similarity scores (detection mode)",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "invalidations": {
      "name": "invalidations",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Winner/loser pairs invalidated or previewed (resolve mode)",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_maintenance_status

Summary: perseus_vault_maintenance_status

#952: read-only maintenance/serving isolation observability. Reports the off-peak maintenance window (configured value, whether it is open now, parse errors), the live-recall SLO budget (PERSEUS_VAULT_MAINTENANCE_P95_BUDGET_MS, last probe latency), the execution-slot state (one maintenance run at a time; held = an operator-explicit run is executing), and lifetime counters (runs started / refused by the gate / mid-run SLO pauses). Maintenance is serialized, never reserved (a disabled mode consumes zero capacity), and gated by window+budget unless force:true — see docs/specs/maintenance-serving-isolation.md.

      "description": "Execution slot: held (bool) and the operation holding it, if any."

    "slo": {
      "name": "slo",
      "type": "object",
      "description": "Live-recall SLO budget ms (PERSEUS_VAULT_MAINTENANCE_P95_BUDGET_MS; null = guard off) and the last measured recall probe latency."

      "type": "object",

  }

##### TOOL perseus_vault_consolidate

Summary: Consolidate Overlapping Facts into Observations

Merge overlapping/duplicative entities in the same category into durable, evidence-tracked 'observations' — the mirror image of perseus_vault_conflicts, which flags dissimilar (contradictory) pairs. Groups entities whose pairwise trigram similarity meets similarity_threshold, then creates one new entity per group (category='observation') whose body carries a summary (the highest-certainty source's content), exact-quote evidence refs (source id + verbatim quote, capped by quote_cap_chars), the full list of source entity ids as evidence, a proof_count, updated_at, a staleness flag, and (on contradiction) a preserved journey in history. The observation links back to each source (relationship='evidence_for') for full audit. #884: with refine_existing (default true), new evidence FOLDS into the best-matching existing observation (proof_count grows, no duplicates) and contradictions reconcile into its journey — 'was React, switched to Vue' — with raw facts intact for trace-back; fold/refine writes go through the audited re-assert path (entity_history snapshot). A staleness refresh pass marks observations stale when newer unconsolidated facts exist. By default sources stay live; set archive_sources=true to retire merged sources of FRESHLY CREATED observations only ('local dreaming' — verified or importance-floored sources are never archived), and cold_first=true to target the memories decay is about to claim. perseus_vault_autocohere runs a bounded cold_first+archive_sources pass automatically. Read-only preview with dry_run=true.

Parameters:
- `archive_sources` (argument, boolean, optional) - Archive merged source entities after the observation is created (archive_reason names the observation; reversible). Verified or importance-floored sources are never archived.
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Category to scan for overlapping/duplicative entities to consolidate
- `cold_first` (argument, boolean, optional) - Scan the COLDEST entities first (longest since last access) instead of the most recent — compress memories that are fading anyway, before decay archives them individually
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Preview which observations would be created without writing anything
- `global` (argument, boolean, optional) - #854 explicit cross-workspace mode for deliberate whole-vault consolidation. Capability-gated (memory.maintenance.global) when the caller carries a host identity. Mutually exclusive with workspace_hash.
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum number of observations to create
- `offset` (argument, integer, optional) - Number of entities to skip for pagination
- `quote_cap_chars` (argument, integer, optional) - #884: cap for exact-quote evidence refs (chars). Quotes are each source's note verbatim, truncated at the cap with an ellipsis marker.
- `refine_existing` (argument, boolean, optional) - #884: fold new evidence into existing observations instead of creating duplicates. Near-duplicate clusters/singletons update the matched observation (proof_count, quotes, updated_at); contradictions are reconciled into its journey (history) rather than blindly overwritten. Folded evidence is never archived.
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Host identity stamped by the MCP transport. Used for global-mode authorization and stamped as author on derived observations.
- `similarity_threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Trigram similarity threshold at or above which two entities are considered overlapping enough to merge
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - #854 workspace scope for this run. Scans, clusters, evidence links, and archive operations are strictly restricted to this workspace, and derived observations inherit it. Mutually exclusive with global=true. One of workspace_hash or global is required.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "entities_examined": {
      "name": "entities_examined",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities scanned in this category"
    },
    "global": {
      "name": "global",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "#854 true when this run deliberately crossed all workspaces"
    },
    "observations": {
      "name": "observations",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "The observations created (or previewed), each with entity_id, key, summary, source_ids, proof_count, certainty",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "observations_created": {
      "name": "observations_created",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of new observation entities created (or would be, in dry-run)"
    },
    "source_entities_merged": {
      "name": "source_entities_merged",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Total count of source entities folded into the created observations"
    },
    "sources_archived": {
      "name": "sources_archived",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Sources archived because archive_sources was set (verified/importance-floored sources are exempt)"
    },
    "workspace_hash": {
      "name": "workspace_hash",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "#854 effective scope: the workspace this run operated in (null when global=true)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_sleep

Summary: Sleep-Cycle Consolidation (Proposal-Only Pass)

#1002: bounded sleep-cycle consolidation without an LLM (CogniCore SleepProcessor borrow). One bounded scan of a category (max_entities, #952 window discipline + maintenance gate) produces PROPOSALS, never silent changes: (1) dedup — pairs at/above similarity_threshold become merge proposals; (2) contradiction — pairs with token overlap PLUS a negation word ('X works' vs 'X does not work') become conflict proposals; (3) optional compression — delegates to perseus_vault_consolidate (cold_first) so fading memories are compressed into evidence-linked observations (the only auto-committed artifact; verified/scored sources exempt). Proposals persist under sleep_proposal.* state keys and surface as the 'sleep' lane of perseus_vault_operator_review for explicit operator decisions. dry_run=true performs the identical work with zero writes.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, required) - Category to scan. The curated mental_model category is refused (curated-only).
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Preview: identical scan and report, zero persisted proposals, zero compression writes
- `force` (argument, boolean, optional) - #952: explicit operator trigger — bypasses the maintenance off-peak window and the live-recall SLO start gate (mid-run pauses still apply).
- `global` (argument, boolean, optional) - #854 deliberate whole-vault mode, capability-gated. Mutually exclusive with workspace_hash.
- `include_compression` (argument, boolean, optional) - Also run the delegated cold_first consolidate pass over the same category (its own maintenance slot; results reported under 'compression')
- `max_entities` (argument, integer, optional) - Scan budget: most-recently-accessed entities examined (clamped 1..=2000)
- `max_proposals` (argument, integer, optional) - Proposal budget: cap on merge+conflict proposals per run (clamped 1..=200)
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Host identity stamped by the MCP transport; used for global-mode authorization.
- `similarity_threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Trigram similarity at or above which two entities are dedup candidates (merge proposal)
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - #854 workspace scope. Mutually exclusive with global=true. One of workspace_hash or global is required.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {
      "name": "category",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "compression": {
      "name": "compression",
      "description": "Delegated consolidate report, or null when include_compression is false"
    },
    "conflict_proposals": {
      "name": "conflict_proposals",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Negation-shaped conflict proposals found (kind=conflict)"
    },
    "dedup_proposals": {
      "name": "dedup_proposals",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Merge proposals found (kind=merge)"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "maintenance_guard": {
      "name": "maintenance_guard",
      "description": "#952 maintenance-window status for this run"
    },
    "proposals": {
      "name": "proposals",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "description": "SleepProposal: kind, category, entity_a, entity_b, similarity, reason, workspace_hash, status"
      }
    },
    "scanned": {
      "name": "scanned",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Entities examined in this run"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_dream

Summary: Dream: LLM Consolidation of Episodic Memory into Semantic Insights

Sleep-time LLM consolidation: batch clusters of related cold/episodic memories, reflect over each cluster via the configured LLM endpoint, and write back durable higher-order SEMANTIC insights (category='insight', semantic layer) — 'given these N memories, what stable pattern/preference/fact do they collectively imply?'. Each written insight carries evidence_for links to every source entity (full provenance), a certainty blended from LLM confidence and evidence coverage, and derivation='dream' so it is auditable and reversible. Idempotent: insights are keyed by an evidence-set hash, so re-dreaming an unchanged cluster never spawns duplicates. Contradictory sources surface as a flagged 'contradiction' insight, never a silent merge. Never fabricates: clusters that support no durable generalization are a no-op. Requires --llm-endpoint (fully local via Ollama); returns a clean error without it unless fallback_consolidate=true, which runs the non-LLM perseus_vault_consolidate pass instead. Bounded by max_entities/max_clusters budgets. Preview with dry_run=true.

Parameters:
- `archive_sources` (argument, boolean, optional) - Archive source entities once an insight citing them is written (archive_reason names the insight; reversible). Verified or importance-floored sources are never archived; contradiction sources always stay live.
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Category to dream over. Omit to scan all categories (derived categories — insight, observation, synthesis, memories — are always skipped) until the entity budget is exhausted.
- `cold_first` (argument, boolean, optional) - Scan the COLDEST entities first (longest since last access) — consolidate fading memories into durable semantic insights before decay claims them.
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Report candidate insights and their evidence sets without writing anything.
- `fallback_consolidate` (argument, boolean, optional) - When no --llm-endpoint is configured, run the mechanical (non-LLM) perseus_vault_consolidate cold_first pass instead of returning an error.
- `max_clusters` (argument, integer, optional) - Budget cap: maximum clusters sent to the LLM per run (= max LLM calls).
- `max_entities` (argument, integer, optional) - Budget cap: maximum entities scanned per run (across categories).
- `min_cluster_size` (argument, integer, optional) - Minimum memories a cluster needs before it is worth dreaming over.
- `similarity_threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Trigram similarity threshold for grouping RELATED memories into one cluster. Lower than consolidate's 0.6 on purpose: dreaming wants thematic neighborhoods, not near-duplicates.
- `topic_path` (argument, string, optional) - Optional topic_path prefix filter applied to the scan.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "categories_scanned": {
      "name": "categories_scanned",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "clusters_dreamed": {
      "name": "clusters_dreamed",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Clusters actually sent to the LLM this run"
    },
    "contradictions_flagged": {
      "name": "contradictions_flagged",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Insights flagged as contradictions among their sources"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "entities_examined": {
      "name": "entities_examined",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities scanned across all categories this run"
    },
    "fallback": {
      "name": "fallback",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Present only when fallback_consolidate ran (no LLM endpoint): always \"consolidate\". The report then has this union shape — categories_scanned, entities_examined, observations_created, sources_archived, dry_run — instead of the LLM dream counters."
    },
    "global": {
      "name": "global",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "#854 true when this run deliberately crossed all workspaces"
    },
    "insights": {
      "name": "insights",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "The insights written (or previewed), each with entity_id, key, summary, insight_type, confidence, source_ids, category, contradiction, deduped",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "insights_deduped": {
      "name": "insights_deduped",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Insights skipped because the identical evidence set was already dreamed"
    },
    "insights_written": {
      "name": "insights_written",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Semantic insights written (or that would be, in dry-run)"
    },
    "note": {
      "name": "note",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Fallback-only explanation of why the mechanical pass ran"
    },
    "observations_created": {
      "name": "observations_created",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Fallback-only: observations created by the mechanical consolidate pass"
    },
    "sources_archived": {
      "name": "sources_archived",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Sources archived because archive_sources was set (verified/importance-floored sources are exempt)"
    },
    "workspace_hash": {
      "name": "workspace_hash",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ],
      "description": "#854 effective scope: the workspace this run operated in (null when global=true)"
    }
  }
}

##### TOOL perseus_vault_seal

Summary: Seal: Tamper Evidence for Persisted Memory

Record a seal (SHA-256 commitment) over a live entity's stored content — hash + label only, never the content itself. Compare-on-recall and perseus_vault_tamper_scan surface any later mismatch as a tamper event naming the entity, so a tampered store is never served silently. Integrity != truth: a seal proves unchanged-since-sealed, never true-when-written.

Parameters:
- `agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Sealing agent identity for the audit trail.
- `label` (argument, string, optional) - Human-readable label recorded with the seal.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_typed_traversal

Summary: Intent-Aware Typed-Relational Traversal

Intent-aware typed-relational traversal (#1065, MAGMA pattern): routes the query to one relation view (temporal / causal / entity / semantic) via a deterministic classifier, runs that view's traversal policy, and returns the explainable selected path (steps carry the relation they were taken over) plus rejected distractors with reasons — with token accounting for the context-budget discipline. LLM-free and reproducible: identical query → identical route.

Parameters:
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Selected-path size bound (1-50, default 10).
- `query` (argument, string, required)

      "name": "query",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "rejected": {
      "name": "rejected",
      "type": "array"
    },
    "run_id": {
      "name": "run_id",
      "type": "string"

      "name": "tokens_rejected",

##### TOOL perseus_vault_vault_import

Summary: Import Vault from Files

Import .md files from a vault directory into the database. Reads YAML frontmatter for metadata and markdown body for content. Idempotent — re-running on the same vault won't duplicate entities. Pass shadow_workspace to run a shadow import: every entity is forced into that scratch workspace and the live bank is never touched, so you can compare recall before cutting over (see perseus_vault_shadow_compare / _promote / _rollback). Pair with perseus_vault_vault_export for transfer.

Parameters:
- `shadow_workspace` (argument, string, optional) - #951 shadow import: when set, every imported entity is forced into this workspace regardless of frontmatter. Zero writes to the live bank; rerunnable with zero new identities.
- `vault_dir` (argument, string, optional) - Directory path to read .md files from. Use ~ for home directory.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "completed_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "completed_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Completion timestamp"
    },
    "errors": {
      "name": "errors",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Any errors encountered during import",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "files_created": {
      "name": "files_created",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of new entities created from files"
    },
    "files_updated": {
      "name": "files_updated",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of existing entities updated"
    },
    "vault_dir": {
      "name": "vault_dir",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Absolute path of the vault directory read"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_shadow_compare

Summary: Compare Live vs Shadow Recall

#951: recall comparison between the live workspace and a shadow workspace over a fixed query set. Deterministic (Fts5 mode), side-effect-free, machine-readable — the gate for deciding whether a shadow import clears cutover.

Parameters:
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Recall limit per query (1..=100).
- `live_workspace` (argument, string, optional) - Live workspace to compare against; omit for the unscoped bank.
- `queries` (argument, array, required) - Fixed query set to run in both workspaces (1..=500).
- `shadow_workspace` (argument, string, required) - The scratch workspace holding the shadow import.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_shadow_promote

Summary: Promote Shadow Import to Live

#951: promote — move every non-archived entity from the shadow workspace into the target workspace in ONE atomic operation, journaling the moved ids so perseus_vault_shadow_rollback can undo the cutover in one operation. dry_run previews the count without writing.

Parameters:
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Preview the move (count only — nothing written, no journal).
- `shadow_workspace` (argument, string, required) - The scratch workspace to promote from.
- `target_workspace` (argument, string, optional) - Target workspace (default: the unscoped live bank).

##### TOOL perseus_vault_shadow_rollback

Summary: Roll Back Shadow Promote

#951: rollback — one operation returns every promoted id to its pre-promote workspace, using the shadow_promote_last journal. dry_run previews the journal without writing.

Parameters:
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - Preview the journal (nothing written, journal kept).

##### TOOL perseus_vault_decay

Summary: Recalculate Decay Scores

Recalculate Ebbinghaus decay scores for all entities based on time since last access. Auto-archives entities that have fully decayed (score < 0.05). Run periodically to keep memory fresh — decayed entities surface less often in recall results.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "auto_archived": {
      "name": "auto_archived",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Entities auto-archived because decay fell below 0.05"
    },
    "completed_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "completed_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Completion timestamp"
    },
    "entities_checked": {
      "name": "entities_checked",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Total entities evaluated"
    },
    "entities_updated": {
      "name": "entities_updated",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Entities whose stored decay score was actually rewritten (rows whose recomputed score changed). A steady-state tick reports ~0: unchanged rows are evaluated but not written."
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_cohere

Summary: Run Coherence Grooming

Run an autonomous coherence grooming pass over the memory. Promotes buffer entities to working layer, applies decay, auto-links related entities, and archives stale ones below the decay threshold. Use dry_run=true to preview without making changes.

Parameters:
- `archive_threshold` (argument, number, optional) - Decay score below which entities are auto-archived (default 0.05)
- `cross_scope_k` (argument, integer, optional) - Minimum distinct workspaces before a recurring fact is promoted (default 3, minimum 2)
- `cross_scope_promote` (argument, boolean, optional) - #486: also run cross-scope promotion — a fact independently observed in >= cross_scope_k distinct workspaces is promoted to one global-scope entity with promoted_from links back to the per-scope evidence. Off by default; re-runs are idempotent (the global scope's dedup absorbs them); undo by forgetting the promoted entity.
- `cross_scope_similarity` (argument, number, optional) - Trigram similarity treating two bodies as the same fact across scopes (default 0.7, matching write-time dedup)
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - If true, count what would be done without making changes
- `max_links` (argument, integer, optional) - Maximum auto-links to create (default 20, max 100)
- `promote_threshold` (argument, integer, optional) - Retrieval count threshold for buffer to working promotion (default 3)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "archived": {
      "name": "archived",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities archived due to low decay"
    },
    "completed_at_unix_ms": {
      "name": "completed_at_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "cross_scope_clusters": {
      "name": "cross_scope_clusters",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "#486: clusters found spanning >= cross_scope_k workspaces (0 unless cross_scope_promote)"
    },
    "cross_scope_promoted": {
      "name": "cross_scope_promoted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "#486: new global-scope entities created by cross-scope promotion"
    },
    "cross_scope_skipped_existing": {
      "name": "cross_scope_skipped_existing",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "#486: qualifying clusters already represented at the global scope (idempotent re-run)"
    },
    "decayed": {
      "name": "decayed",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities whose decay score was reduced"
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "name": "dry_run",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "entities_examined": {
      "name": "entities_examined",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Total non-archived entities examined"
    },
    "linked": {
      "name": "linked",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of auto-links created"
    },
    "promoted": {
      "name": "promoted",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Number of entities promoted from buffer to working"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_autocohere

Summary: Atomic Coherence Pass

Run a full atomic grooming pass. When capture_text is supplied, capture runs first and must succeed before cohere, decay, compact, consolidation, or retention can compress source context. Returns a summary report. Use dry_run=true to preview without writing.

Parameters:
- `capture_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Agent attribution for pre-compaction captured facts

- `capture_workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope for pre-compaction captured facts
- `dry_run` (argument, boolean, optional) - If true, preview changes without writing
- `global` (argument, boolean, optional) - #854 explicit whole-vault consolidation mode (capability-gated with a host identity). Mutually exclusive with workspace_hash.
- `requesting_agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Host identity stamped by the MCP transport. Used for global-mode authorization and consolidation author attribution.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - #854 workspace scope for the consolidation step. When set, only that workspace's entities are consolidated and the observations inherit the scope. Omit for the whole-vault pass.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_supersede

Summary: Supersede Entity

Create a 'supersedes' relationship from a new fact to an old one, setting the old entity's status to 'deprecated'. Use this when a newer entity makes an older one obsolete.

Parameters:
- `from_category` (argument, string, required) - Category of the OLD entity being superseded
- `from_key` (argument, string, required) - Key of the OLD entity being superseded
- `reason` (argument, string, optional) - Reason for superseding (recorded in archive_reason)
- `relationship` (argument, string, optional) - Link relationship type (default: 'supersedes')
- `to_category` (argument, string, required) - Category of the NEW entity that supersedes
- `to_key` (argument, string, required) - Key of the NEW entity that supersedes
- `valid_to_unix_ms` (argument, integer, optional) - When the OLD fact stopped being true in the world (#363, unix ms). Defaults to transaction time (now). Closes the old entity's application-time period so perseus_vault_valid_at stops returning it from that instant on. Must be after the fact's valid_from, and may only TIGHTEN an already-closed period (a fact that ended cannot be retroactively extended); violations are rejected before any mutation.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {

      "type": "string",

    },
    "from_entity_key": {
      "name": "from_entity_key",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "from_valid_to_unix_ms": {
      "name": "from_valid_to_unix_ms",
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "The instant the old fact's validity was closed at (#363)"
    },
    "relationship": {
      "name": "relationship",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "status_updated": {
      "name": "status_updated",
      "type": "string",
      "description": "New status of the old entity (always 'deprecated')"
    },
    "to_entity_category": {

##### TOOL perseus_vault_consistency_audit

Summary: Consistency Audit (court of record)

Read-only court-of-record self-audit (#940): scans the category for contradiction pairs, recommends a deterministic winner per pair (importance → source-authority → recency → id), surfaces pairs with an existing active ruling, lists supersession lag (deprecated entities without a live successor), and reports the pending keystone suggestion count. NEVER mutates: run before ruling, decide with perseus_vault_audit_ruling.

Parameters:
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Category to audit (default: facts)
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max contradiction pairs to scan (clamped 1-200, default 50)

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "findings": {
      "name": "findings",
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Per-pair: recommendation {winner_id, winner_key, decided_by} or already_ruled {ruling_id, winner_id}"
    },
    "keystone_pending": {
      "name": "keystone_pending",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "read_only": {
      "name": "read_only",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "Always true — the audit never mutates"
    },
    "supersession_lag": {
      "name": "supersession_lag",
      "type": "array"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_audit_ruling

Summary: Audit Ruling (court of record)

Idempotent operator ruling over a consistency finding (#940): accept compiles the recommended winner into the supersede guard (winner→loser link, loser valid-period closed, status deprecated); override compiles an explicit winner; reverse reopens a ruled pair for re-litigation (the compiled guard remains). Rulings are recorded + journaled (court_ruling_set/court_ruling_reversed); an active ruling with a different winner is refused until reversed.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, required) - accept = compile the ladder-recommended winner; override = compile an explicit winner; reverse = reopen a ruled pair
- `category` (argument, string, optional) - Category of entity_a/entity_b (default: facts)
- `decided_by` (argument, string, optional) - Who decided (default: operator)
- `entity_a_key` (argument, string, optional) - Key of the first contested entity (accept/override)
- `entity_b_key` (argument, string, optional) - Key of the second contested entity (accept/override)
- `rationale` (argument, string, optional) - Optional ruling rationale (recorded verbatim)
- `ruling_id` (argument, string, optional) - Reverse only: id of the active ruling to reopen
- `winner_category` (argument, string, optional) - Override only: category of the explicit winner
- `winner_key` (argument, string, optional) - Override only: key of the explicit winner

##### TOOL perseus_vault_communities

Summary: Detect Link-Graph Communities

GraphRAG community detection: partition the entity link graph (built via perseus_vault_link) into communities using deterministic label propagation or greedy modularity ('louvain'). Persists the result with an extractive summary per community; community ids are derived from the member set, so re-detection after membership changes yields new ids. Local-first — no LLM or network required.

Parameters:
- `algorithm` (argument, string, optional) - Detection algorithm: 'label_prop' (deterministic label propagation, default) or 'louvain' (greedy one-level modularity optimization).
- `min_size` (argument, integer, optional) - Minimum member count for a community to be kept (minimum 2 — isolated entities never form communities).
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope for the graph. Empty = global/unscoped entities.

      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "id": {
            "name": "id",
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Community id ('com-' + member-set digest)"
          },
          "member_ids": {
            "name": "member_ids",
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "size": {
            "name": "size",
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "summary": {
            "name": "summary",
            "type": "string",

        }

      "name": "edge_count",

      "type": "integer"

##### TOOL perseus_vault_global_recall

Cites entities across multiple communities instead of returning only the single nearest cluster like flat recall. Detects communities automatically on first use. Local-first and deterministic; optional use_llm synthesizes the final answer.

Parameters:
- `auto_detect` (argument, boolean, optional) - Run community detection automatically when none are persisted yet
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max member entities cited across all communities (round-robined so every matched community is represented)
- `query` (argument, string, required) - The global question to answer across the whole memory graph
- `top_communities` (argument, integer, optional) - How many best-matching communities to drill into
- `use_llm` (argument, boolean, optional) - Synthesize the final answer with the configured LLM; degrades to the extractive answer on error or when disabled.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Workspace scope. Empty = global/unscoped entities.

Returns:
```json

  "properties": {

    },

      "name": "communities",
      "type": "array",

        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "id": {
            "name": "id",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "members": {
            "name": "members",
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "category": {
                  "name": "category",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "id": {
                  "name": "id",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "key": {
                  "name": "key",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "score": {
                  "name": "score",
                  "type": "number"
                },
                "snippet": {
                  "name": "snippet",
                  "type": "string"
                }
              }
            }
          },
          "score": {
            "name": "score",
            "type": "number",
            "description": "Distinct query-token hits in the community summary"
          },
          "size": {

          }

##### TOOL perseus_vault_keystone_set

Summary: Set Keystone

Author a Keystone — a mandatory policy rule that survives context compaction (#683). Unlike ordinary memories (retrieved when relevant), keystones are fetched deterministically at session start via perseus_vault_keystone_get, merged across scope, and are meant to be obeyed over any conflicting instruction (e.g. 'Every memory write MUST carry a retention class', 'Customer PII MUST NOT cross agent boundaries'). Higher weight wins on contradiction. Re-setting the same (scope, scope_id, content) updates it in place. Every mutation is appended to the cryptographic audit chain. Authoring is gated on trust tier: pass author_trust_tier (>= trust_tier_required, default 2). NOTE: until multi-agent trust tiers land (#684), author_trust_tier is caller-asserted; when omitted the write is allowed and the response flags that enforcement is pending.

Parameters:
- `agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Identity of the authoring agent, stamped on the keystone and its audit-chain event for provenance.
- `author_trust_tier` (argument, integer, optional) - The authoring agent's trust tier, checked against trust_tier_required. Caller-asserted until #684 wires per-agent trust + session identity.
- `content` (argument, string, required) - The policy rule text. Imperative, testable directives work best.
- `scope` (argument, string, optional) - Merge scope: 'tenant' (org-wide), 'fleet' (a team), or 'agent' (an individual). Narrower scopes are layered on top of broader ones at get time.
- `scope_id` (argument, string, optional) - Identifier the keystone applies to within a non-tenant scope: the fleet_id ('fleet') or agent_id ('agent'). Omit/empty for tenant scope or 'all in scope'.
- `trust_tier_required` (argument, integer, optional) - Minimum author trust tier permitted to set/modify this keystone. Defaults to 2 (per #684's tier model: tier 2 = write keystones).
- `weight` (argument, number, optional) - Conflict-resolution weight; on contradiction the higher-weight keystone wins. Also the merge/sort order returned by keystone_get.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Optional workspace scope. Keystones with an empty workspace_hash are global (apply everywhere).

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "created": {
      "name": "created",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "true if a new keystone was created, false if an existing one was updated"
    },
    "id": {
      "name": "id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "trust_enforced": {
      "name": "trust_enforced",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "false when author_trust_tier was omitted (enforcement pending #684)"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_keystone_get

Summary: Get Keystones

Fetch the merged Keystones (mandatory policy rules, #683) that apply at session start — the deterministic counterpart to recall. Returns rules ordered by weight (highest first, then scope tenant<fleet<agent, then id) so a renderer can inject them ahead of all other context and resolve contradictions by weight. Filter by scope/scope_id/workspace to get exactly the set an agent must obey. Read-only.

Parameters:
- `scope` (argument, string, optional) - Optional: restrict to a single scope ('tenant' | 'fleet' | 'agent'). Omit to merge all scopes.
- `scope_id` (argument, string, optional) - Optional: with a non-tenant scope, restrict to this fleet_id/agent_id. Rules with an empty scope_id (scope-wide) are always included.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Optional workspace scope. Global keystones (empty workspace_hash) are always included.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "count": {
      "name": "count",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "keystones": {
      "name": "keystones",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "content": {
            "name": "content",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "id": {
            "name": "id",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "scope": {
            "name": "scope",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "scope_id": {
            "name": "scope_id",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "weight": {
            "name": "weight",
            "type": "number"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_keystone_suggestions

Summary: List Keystone Suggestions

List candidate directive/keystone suggestions (#889) extracted from `correct` captures by word-boundary-anchored patterns (en/de/ru/it/es). Suggestions are candidates only — never policy: promotion to the keystones table requires an explicit operator `approve` decision via perseus_vault_keystone_suggestion_decide. Each suggestion carries its source correction entity id for citation. Filter by status (pending/approved/rejected) and workspace; read-only.

Parameters:
- `limit` (argument, integer, optional) - Max rows (1-1000). Default 50.
- `status` (argument, string, optional) - Filter: '' (all), 'pending', 'approved', or 'rejected'. Default ''.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Optional workspace scope filter.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "count": {
      "name": "count",
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "suggestions": {
      "name": "suggestions",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_keystone_suggestion_decide

Summary: Decide Keystone Suggestion

Decide a keystone-suggestion candidate (#889): 'approve' promotes the suggestion's instruction into the keystones table (re-running the #683/#684 trust-tier gate — authoring requires tier >= trust_tier_required) and marks the suggestion approved; 'reject' marks it rejected and writes nothing. Extraction never writes policy — this explicit operator decision is the only promotion path.

Parameters:
- `action` (argument, string, required) - 'approve' (promote to keystone) or 'reject'.
- `agent_id` (argument, string, optional) - Author agent id (registry-backed tier wins when registered).
- `author_trust_tier` (argument, integer, optional) - Caller-asserted tier (used when the agent is not registry-registered).
- `id` (argument, string, required) - Suggestion id (ksug-...).
- `scope` (argument, string, optional) - Keystone scope: 'tenant' | 'fleet' | 'agent'. Default 'agent'.
- `scope_id` (argument, string, optional) - Keystone scope_id; defaults to agent_id.
- `trust_tier_required` (argument, integer, optional) - Minimum authoring tier. Default 2.
- `weight` (argument, number, optional) - Conflict-resolution weight. Default 1.0.
- `workspace_hash` (argument, string, optional) - Must match the suggestion's own workspace.

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "keystone_id": {
      "name": "keystone_id",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ok": {
      "name": "ok",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "suggestion_status": {
      "name": "suggestion_status",
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_agent

Summary: Agent Registry

Register/update or look up an agent in the multi-agent registry (#684). Agents carry a trust tier (0-3) that gates sensitive ops (e.g. authoring keystones needs tier >= 2) and drives visibility enforcement on recall: tier 0 = read own only, 1 = fleet, 2 = read all + write keystones, 3 = admin. Pass trust_tier (and optionally name/fleet_id) to upsert; omit trust_tier to just look up. entities/journal already stamp agent_id (v1.2.0); this adds the identity + tier metadata. NOTE: an empty/unknown agent has no registry row — unknown identified agents resolve to tier 0, and a caller with no session identity is unscoped.

Parameters:
- `agent_id` (argument, string, required) - The agent's stable identifier (e.g. the MCP clientInfo name).
- `fleet_id` (argument, string, optional) - Fleet/team the agent belongs to (used for 'fleet' visibility). Upsert only.
- `name` (argument, string, optional) - Human-readable name (upsert only).
- `trust_tier` (argument, integer, optional) - Trust tier 0-3. Provide to upsert; omit to look up. Clamped to [0,3].

Returns:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "agent": {
      "name": "agent",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "agent_id": {
          "name": "agent_id",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "fleet_id": {
          "name": "fleet_id",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "name": {
          "name": "name",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "trust_tier": {
          "name": "trust_tier",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      }
    },
    "created": {
      "name": "created",
      "type": "boolean",
      "description": "true if an upsert created a new registry row"
    },
    "found": {
      "name": "found",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  }
}
```

##### TOOL perseus_vault_action_approve

Summary: Decide Action Approval

Grant or deny an approval-requested action.

##### TOOL perseus_vault_report_refusal

Summary: Report Refusal (Retry Payload)

Extraction-loss net (#1048): an answerer's refusal over a served payload is evidence. Re-scores the served entities' residual spans against the original query and returns a retry payload (spans whose query-similarity beats the entity's own by a margin — the anomaly rule). Units with no retry material accumulate lossy marks; at the threshold they are flagged for repair-on-touch.

Parameters:
- `query` (argument, string, required) - The query the answerer could not answer
- `reason` (argument, string, optional) - Optional refusal reason (kept for the journal)
- `served_ids` (argument, array, required) - Entity ids that were in the served payload

      }

      "name": "margin",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "retry": {
      "name": "retry",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "retry_n": {
      "name": "retry_n",

}
